statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. The U.S. session remains upward with NQ in the upper part of its range and broad cash-index gains, but semiconductor confirmation is weaker and repeated failed retracements are not verified.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail remains below the blocking threshold because the available path evidence does not establish repeated extension after failed pullbacks; Stress remains extreme ahead of Friday's Employment Situation.
headline: WATCH as Nasdaq strength remains broad but not fully confirmed by semiconductors
body: Delayed NQ is around 29,321 versus a 29,207 open and a roughly 29,376 session high. Reuters reports the Nasdaq up about 1.2% as yields ease, while chipmakers lag broader technology leadership. Oil near six-week highs and unresolved Middle East supply risk keep Stress extreme ahead of Friday payrolls.

lookbackSummary: Published Tail was mostly low overnight, rose through the U.S. macro sequence, and reached WATCH during the U.S. session. The 2026-09-02 22:00 UTC slot remains unavailable.
outlookSummary: The immediate checkpoint is whether the afternoon advance keeps extending near session highs or produces meaningful pullbacks. Hammack's 19:00 UTC remarks are a medium event checkpoint; Friday's 12:30 UTC Employment Situation is the next major high-Stress window.

forecast.analysis: Delayed NQ is around 29,321, above the 29,207 open and within roughly 55 points of the 29,376 session high. Nasdaq cash is up about 1.2%, while chip leadership is weaker than broad megacaps; the session is upward, but repeated failed retracements are not verified.
drivers: NQ remains in the upper part of today's range
Megacap gains are broad while semiconductors lag
Oil and Hormuz risk keep Stress extreme

forecast.analysis: If the afternoon rally keeps making higher highs but still permits meaningful pullbacks, Tail remains in WATCH rather than escalating. A fresh high followed by shallow retracements and renewed extension would be the key contrary condition.

news.title: Wall St climbs after Fed's Waller says he could support rate hold

forecast.analysis: Hammack's scheduled 19:00 UTC opening remarks create a medium event checkpoint. Tail stays in WATCH unless the subsequent NQ response becomes directionally persistent, holds an extreme and resists meaningful retracement.

Around the cash close, Tail falls to low if the speaker window and earlier rally are absorbed through two-way trade. Persistent closing extension with broad technology confirmation would keep the path more directional than this baseline.
Post-close liquidity can widen individual moves, but low Tail assumes no sustained directional extension. Friday payroll proximity keeps Stress extreme even if the price path becomes quieter.

During the futures maintenance transition, Tail remains low absent a new geopolitical shock or a one-way reopening gap. Thin liquidity by itself is treated mainly as Stress rather than evidence of failed mean reversion.

news.title: Oil prices hit fresh 6-week highs on renewed Middle East tensions

forecast.analysis: Early evening futures trade is expected to be lower-information. Tail remains low unless a persistent direction forms and repeatedly survives pullbacks as liquidity rebuilds.

The first full overnight hour carries low Tail in the baseline. A material gap tied to verified geopolitical escalation would raise risk only if the price path then extends without meaningful retracement.

news.title: Oil prices hit fresh 6-week highs on renewed Middle East tensions

forecast.analysis: With the U.S. employment report still many hours away, Tail remains low if overnight futures rotate normally. Stress stays extreme because payroll and oil risks remain unresolved.

Low-liquidity overnight conditions can produce noise, but the baseline remains low Tail. A move becomes more consequential only if it develops persistent directional efficiency rather than isolated volatility.
Tail remains low through the deeper overnight period provided neither geopolitical news nor a sustained futures trend produces repeated extension after failed pullbacks.
As Asian trading develops, Tail remains low in the baseline. Cross-asset alignment would matter only if it coincides with persistent NQ structure rather than simply higher volatility.

Approaching the European morning, Stress rises while Tail stays low. Any overnight directional move needs to preserve shallow pullbacks and hold near extremes before it would justify a higher Tail state.
European participation raises liquidity and cross-asset information. Tail remains low unless NQ, rates and technology leadership align with a sustained directional move that resists retracement.

As U.S. premarket participation begins to build, the baseline still assumes two-way price discovery. Stress is extreme because the Employment Situation is approaching, but event importance alone does not lift Tail above low.

news.title: US labor market remains stable; services input price rises point to elevated inflation

forecast.analysis: Two-way premarket structure keeps Tail at the top of low. A large gap would be treated as Stress unless it is accompanied by repeated extension and shallow or failed retracements.
Within four hours of payrolls, Stress is extreme and mode shifts toward event/whipsaw. Tail remains low because the release outcome and post-release path are not yet observed.
drivers: No future price path is treated as observed

news.title: US labor market remains stable; services input price rises point to elevated inflation

forecast.analysis: The final pre-release hours move Tail into WATCH as liquidity and positioning can become less stable. A blocking state still requires subsequently observed directional persistence rather than anticipation of the data alone.

One hour before the Employment Situation, Tail is WATCH and Stress is extreme. The key condition is whether pre-release positioning remains two-way or begins to form a persistent directional structure.

The 12:30 UTC Employment Situation falls inside this hour. Tail is WATCH before the result; any higher state depends on the observed post-release path, especially repeated extension, extreme holding and failed retracements.

The first full post-payroll hour remains WATCH in the conditional baseline. Tail would rise only if actual price discovery shows sustained one-way movement with poor retracement quality; orderly two-way discovery would reduce it.
drivers: Orderly two-way discovery would lower Tail

forecast.analysis: As the U.S. cash open approaches, WATCH persists because payroll repricing can carry into the opening auction. The main checkpoint is whether the opening move extends repeatedly or instead mean-reverts.
After the opening transition, Tail eases within WATCH if payroll-driven volatility produces meaningful counter-swings. Persistent same-direction extension would be the contrary condition.

By the later morning, the baseline expects payroll information to be more absorbed. Tail remains at the bottom of WATCH unless a delayed second leg emerges with aligned rates, technology breadth and weak retracements.

forecastDetail.comment: Current delayed NQ is in the upper session range with broad cash-index strength, but semiconductor confirmation and failed-retracement evidence remain incomplete.
WATCH persists conditionally if the rally holds while still allowing meaningful pullbacks; shallow repeated pullbacks would be the escalation signal.
Hammack's 19:00 UTC remarks are a medium checkpoint; only the observed subsequent price path can change Tail materially.
Low Tail around the cash close assumes two-way absorption rather than continued closing extension.
Post-close volatility alone is not Tail; sustained directional extension is the relevant checkpoint.
Maintenance-hour liquidity is thin, but Tail stays low absent a one-way reopening gap or geopolitical discontinuity.
